key_insight: Guidance for diffusion and flow generative models can break probability conservation and push samples off the learned manifold; this paper derives a continuity-equation view and introduces a probability-conserving flow guidance that corrects guidance vector fields to preserve mass and stay on-manifold.
problem_solved: Existing guidance heuristics (e.g., Classifier-Free Guidance and extrapolation) ignore generative-manifold geometry and the continuity equation, causing probability leakage and degraded or unstable samples under strong guidance.
method: Analyze guidance through the continuity equation to identify how naive linear combinations of velocities/scores create divergence (probability loss) and manifold drift.
Derive a correction to the guidance vector field that enforces probability conservation (zero net divergence) so guided dynamics remain consistent with the learned generative distribution.

Provide a plug-and-play flow-guidance algorithm applicable to flow- and diffusion-based samplers that preserves probability mass with low extra compute and improves robustness at high guidance strengths.
impact: By enforcing probability conservation during guidance, practitioners get more stable, on-manifold controlled sampling and higher-fidelity conditional generation even with strong guidance — usable as a drop-in improvement for diffusion and flow pipelines.
visual_elements: Schematic comparing vector fields: (a) standard CFG/extrapolation with divergent arrows leaving manifold, (b) probability-conserving corrected field with arrows flowing along manifold.
Illustration of the continuity equation: probability density evolution under guidance, showing how divergence creates mass loss and how the correction restores conservation.
Manifold sketch with sample trajectories: uncorrected guidance that departs from manifold vs corrected guidance that stays on-manifold.
Metric chart: sample quality / fidelity or stability vs guidance strength, showing reduced degradation when using probability-conserving guidance.
paper_authors: Parsa Esmati, Junha Hyung, Amirhossein Dadashzadeh, Jaegul Choo, Majid Mirmehdi
